title: Design patterns in practice
summary: Pick the structure a requirement calls for, and know when a pattern is overkill. Judged on fit, not on naming patterns.

questions.prompt: Checkout must support several discount rules (percentage off, buy-one-get-one, none) chosen per customer, with more coming.
options: Strategy: a PricingRule interface with one implementation per rule, passed into checkout
A switch on a discount-type string inside checkout
A Singleton holding the current discount

questions.prompt: When an order ships, email, analytics and loyalty points must all react, and teams keep adding reactions.
options: Observer: the order publishes a Shipped event; listeners subscribe
Call each service directly from ship()

questions.prompt: Your code expects a PaymentGateway interface, but the vendor SDK has different method names and types.
options: Adapter: a class implementing PaymentGateway that translates calls to the SDK
Copy SDK calls throughout the codebase

questions.prompt: A data stream sometimes needs compression, sometimes encryption, sometimes both, in either order.
options: Decorator: wrappers that each add one behaviour and can be stacked
Boolean flags inside the stream class

questions.prompt: What is the main drawback of a Singleton for something like a database connection pool?
options: It's hidden global state: hard to replace in tests and couples every caller to one instance

questions.prompt: A vending machine behaves differently when idle, holding money or sold out. When does the State pattern beat if/else checks?
options: When states and transitions grow, so each state's behaviour lives in its own object

questions.prompt: Which change best follows 'open for extension, closed for modification'?
options: Adding a new PricingRule class without editing Checkout
Adding another case to a switch in Checkout

questions.prompt: Why prefer composition over inheritance for sharing behaviour?
options: Behaviour can be combined and swapped at runtime, and classes aren't locked into one rigid hierarchy
